paragraphs: I’m a software engineer and a B.Tech graduate of Lovely Professional University (2020 – 2024).

At Stackly I joined as a Software Engineer building Java and Spring Boot APIs for the ONE Enterprise Cloud Platform, then moved up to Lead Software Engineer — leading a 12-member backend team and owning sprint planning, API design and role-based access control across the HRMS, ERP, CRM and Finance modules.

Outside work I build systems end to end: TopCoders, a live coding platform with per-user code sandboxes on AWS Fargate, and SearchForge, a web search engine written from scratch in Java. Before Stackly I interned at Mind Sparc Innovations and ScrollAR4U Technologies.

projects.name: Top Coders
projects.summary: A LeetCode-style platform with a browser IDE, hidden-test judging, monthly hackathons and real-time leaderboards.
projects.overview:
Top Coders is a full-stack competitive programming platform where users solve problems in C++, Java, Python or JavaScript right in the browser. Every submission runs against hidden tests in an isolated sandbox, and results feed into monthly hackathons and real-time leaderboards ranked by points and penalty time.

I designed and built the whole system end to end: the React front end with the Monaco editor, the Node.js and Express API, MongoDB data model, the per-user code runners on AWS ECS Fargate, and the CI/CD pipeline that deploys it.
points: Architected and deployed a coding platform supporting 4 languages (C++, Java, Python, JavaScript) with a browser IDE, hidden-test judging, monthly hackathons, and real-time leaderboards ranked by points and penalty time.
Engineered an on-demand, per-user code sandbox on AWS ECS Fargate with auto-shutdown on idle, logout or tab close, cutting execution compute costs by 92% (~$40 → ~$3/month).
Implemented secure authentication and RBAC: JWT with token-version revocation, bcrypt hashing, email verification, password reset and per-user rate limiting.
Automated AWS infrastructure (IAM, ECR, ECS, ALB, ACM, SSM) and a GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline running 55 unit, API and end-to-end tests against real MongoDB and runner containers.

projects.name: SearchForge
projects.summary: A web search engine written from first principles in Java 21 — no Lucene, no Elasticsearch.
projects.overview:
SearchForge is a complete web search engine built without search libraries: it crawls the web politely, builds a compressed index, ranks results by relevance and link popularity, and serves them through a fast React interface.

The crawler collects 48 pages per second across 120 websites while following each site’s robots.txt rules. A batch pipeline splits indexing into parallel tasks, a custom compression scheme cuts index storage by 76%, and ranking that combines text matching with PageRank over 100,000+ links scores 84% on a standard ranking-quality benchmark.
points: Built a polite, resumable web crawler that collects 48 pages per second across 120 websites: RFC 9309 robots.txt parsing, a per-host politeness frontier, virtual-thread workers, an SSRF guard and SimHash near-duplicate detection.
Designed a batch indexing pipeline (external merge sort with sorted runs and a k-way merge) and a custom VByte + d-gap compression scheme that reduced index storage by 76%, with memory-mapped reads.

Ranked results with BM25F (title, headings and body weighted) plus a PageRank prior over 100,000+ links, scoring 84% on a standard ranking-quality benchmark; added phrase and boolean queries and top-K autocomplete.
Added BK-tree “Did you mean?” spelling suggestions that check 98% fewer words per search.
Delivered a Spring Boot API with result caching, per-IP rate limiting and security headers, and a responsive React + TypeScript search UI, with 96–99% line coverage per module enforced by the build.
